subtitle: From Ruined Delhi to a Living Hospice of the Deccan

panels.shot: low-angle medium close-up framed by Deccan arches
panels.action: Bande Nawaz Gesudaraz, aged and luminous, sits beneath a simple Gulbarga arch, one hand resting on a wooden staff, while a line of poor men and women stretches behind him across a dusty courtyard.

dialogue.text: From Timur’s ruined Delhi to Gulbarga’s dust, Bande Nawaz Gesudaraz must decide: can a stranger turn a war-torn Deccan city into a home of food, prayer and language?

i18n.hi: तैमूर की उजड़ी दिल्ली से गुलबर्गा की धूल तक, बांदे नवाज़ गेसूदराज सोचें: क्या बेगाना दक्कन के जंगज़दा शहर को रोटी, दुआ और ज़बान का घर बना सकता है?

panels.shot: wide overhead of medieval Delhi skyline
panels.action: Young Bande Nawaz stands on a flat rooftop in fourteenth-century Delhi, clutching a manuscript, as smoke from distant fires curls over crowded lanes and domes.

dialogue.text: He was born in Delhi in 1321, when it was the beating heart of the Sultanate, its lanes thick with traders, scholars and the songs of Sufis.

i18n.hi: वो १३२१ की दिल्ली में जन्मे, जब सुल्तनत की धड़कन वहीं थी, गलियाँ सौदागरों, उलेमा और सूफियों के कलाम से भरी थीं।

panels.shot: medium shot at ground level amid trudging caravan
panels.action: As a boy, Bande Nawaz walks beside an ox-cart laden with household bundles on the road south, his face turned back toward the receding silhouette of Delhi’s walls.

dialogue.text: When Muhammad bin Tughluq marched families toward Daulatabad, the boy joined that slow river of dust, learning early that power can uproot a city overnight.

i18n.hi: जब मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक ने ख़ानदानों को दौलताबाद की तरफ़ हांक दिया, लड़का भी उस धूल भरी नदी में चला, और जल्दी समझ गया कि ताक़त शहर को एक रात में उखाड़ फेंकती है।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot lit by oil lamp
panels.action: Inside a modest Delhi khanqah, the older Nasiruddin Chiragh Dehlavi is seated on a low cushion while Bande Nawaz, now a serious young man, listens at his feet among other disciples.

dialogue.text: Back in Delhi, he sat before Nasiruddin Chiragh Dehlavi, the Chishti lamp of the city, learning that the path was service, not court rank.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली लौटकर वो नसीरुद्दीन चराग़ देहलवी के आगे बैठे, शहर के चिश्ती चिराग़, जिन्होंने बताया कि रास्ता ख़िदमत है, न कि दरबार की कुर्सी।

panels.shot: close-up on Bande Nawaz’s face, half-lit, with parchment in hand
panels.action: Bande Nawaz leans over a low desk, copying lines onto a manuscript while shelves of Arabic and Persian books loom behind him in a small study.

dialogue.text: He read and wrote in Arabic and Persian, weaving the words of earlier saints into his Jawami-ul-Kilam, yet his master reminded him to keep the door open to the hungry.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने अरबी-फ़ारसी में पढ़ा-लिखा, पुराने औलिया के कलाम बुनकर ‘जवामिउल कलाम’ लिखी, पर उस्ताद याद दिलाते रहे: भूखों के लिए दर खुला रखो।

panels.shot: chaotic wide shot of Delhi street with riders and smoke
panels.action: In a narrow Delhi street, Bande Nawaz clutches his shawl as panicked townspeople rush past and distant mounted soldiers are silhouetted against flickers of burning rooftops.

dialogue.text: Then in 1398, Timur’s forces broke Delhi. Chronicles remember emptied markets, silent mosques, broken houses. For many, it was the end of Delhi’s spell.

i18n.hi: फिर १३९८ में तैमूर की फ़ौजों ने दिल्ली तोड़ दी। तवारीख़ सूने बाज़ार, खामोश मस्जिदें, टूटी छतें याद रखती हैं। बहुतों के लिए दिल्ली का जादू यहीं टूटा।

panels.shot: medium shot inside sparse cell, contemplative
panels.action: Seated alone in a bare room, Bande Nawaz looks at a travel bundle and his staff, while a small map of Hindustan and the Deccan lies unrolled beside him.

dialogue.text: Now in his late seventies, he chose to leave the ruined capital. Chronicles say he turned his steps south again, toward the Deccan and the Bahmani capital at Gulbarga.

i18n.hi: अब सत्तर के पार, उन्होंने उजड़ी राजधानी छोड़ने का फ़ैसला किया। तवारीख़ लिखती हैं कि उन्होंने फिर क़दम दक्कन की तरफ़ मोड़े, बहमनी राजधानी गुलबर्गा की ओर।

panels.shot: wide landscape shot of caravan crossing Deccan plain
panels.action: Bande Nawaz, now visibly elderly, rides a simple donkey at the edge of a small caravan moving across a dry Deccan plain under a hard sky, with scattered trees and distant hills.

dialogue.text: The road to Gulbarga ran through stone outcrops and thorn. With each mile, the memory of Chiragh’s words traveled with him: carry the Delhi lamp wherever you go.

i18n.hi: गुलबर्गा की राह पत्थरीले टीले और काँटों से होकर जाती थी। हर मील पर चराग़ के लफ़्ज़ साथ चलते रहे: जहाँ जाओ, दिल्ली का चिराग़ साथ ले जाओ।

panels.shot: establishing wide shot of Gulbarga city and fort
panels.action: The high walls and domes of Gulbarga rise behind a bustling bazaar where Deccani villagers, soldiers, merchants and mendicants mingle, as Bande Nawaz enters on foot at the city gate.

dialogue.text: By 1399–1400, Gulbarga was young but restless. Bahmani rulers, soldiers from many regions, and local villagers shared its streets, yet its heart still searched for a center of solace.

i18n.hi: १३९९–१४०० तक गुलबर्गा जवान था पर बेचैन। बहमनी बादशाह, तरह–तरह के सिपाही और स्थानीय देहात वाले एक ही गलियों में थे, पर दिल अब भी किसी ठंडी पनाह की तलाश में था।

panels.shot: medium courtly shot in palace hall
panels.action: In a modest palace hall, the Bahmani Sultan Firuz Shah sits on a low throne as Bande Nawaz, simple-robed and calm, stands before him with his staff, courtiers watching curiously.

dialogue.speaker: bande_nawaz_gesudaraz
dialogue.text: Majesty, my palace is any place where the poor can eat and rest.

i18n.hi: हुज़ूर, मेरा महल वहीं है जहाँ ग़रीब पेट भर कर चैन से सो सके।

panels.shot: wide shot of open land outside city
panels.action: On a patch of open ground near Gulbarga’s outskirts, Bande Nawaz stands among a few disciples as laborers raise simple mud walls and plant wooden posts for a new hospice.

dialogue.text: With the Sultan’s respect but not his command, Bande Nawaz chose open land for a khanqah—a hospice that would not mirror the court, but soften its edges.

i18n.hi: सुल्तान की इज़्ज़त तो ली, पर हुक्म नहीं; बांदे नवाज़ ने खुली ज़मीन पर ख़ानकाह चुनी—ऐसी दरगाह जो दरबार की नकल नहीं, उसकी सख़्ती को नरम करे।

panels.shot: busy interior courtyard wide shot
panels.action: Within the completed khanqah courtyard, a long line of men, women and children sits cross-legged as Bande Nawaz ladles steaming food from a large pot, disciples carrying trays among the crowd.

dialogue.text: Soon the hospice became a place where hunger met hot food. Chronicles recall that his kitchen fed the poor daily, turning charity into a steady habit, not a rare spectacle.

i18n.hi: जल्दी ही ख़ानकाह वो जगह बनी जहाँ भूख का सामना गरम खाने से हुआ। तवारीख़ लिखती हैं, उनकी रसोई रोज़ ग़रीबों को खिलाती, सख़ावत को तमाशा नहीं, रोज़ का काम बना दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of two disputants before Bande Nawaz
panels.action: Two men in local dress argue tensely in the courtyard while Bande Nawaz sits between them on a mat, one hand raised gently, listeners gathered around.

dialogue.text: Disputes over land, debt and promises also arrived. In the absence of easy courts, his hospice mediated quarrels, stitching fragile peace between neighbors in the language they spoke.

i18n.hi: ज़मीन, करज़ और वादों के झगड़े भी वहीं चले आए। आसान अदालतें न थीं, तो उनकी ख़ानकाह ने ही सुलह कराई, लोगों की अपनी ज़बान में पड़ोसी–पड़ोसी के बीच नाज़ुक अमन सिल दिया।

panels.shot: intimate teaching circle medium shot
panels.action: Under a shaded verandah, Bande Nawaz sits with a circle of students—some in turbans, some bareheaded—as he gestures gently and a disciple reads from a manuscript.

dialogue.text: His teaching circle grew. He spoke in Persian and Arabic for scholars, but also in the emerging Dakhni for craftsmen and villagers, letting mystical ideas travel in familiar sounds.

i18n.hi: उनकी सुहबत की महफ़िलें बढ़ती गईं। उलेमा से वो फ़ारसी–अरबी में बोलते, मगर कारीगरों और देहातियों से उभरती दख़नी में, ताकि रहस्य की बातें अपने से लगने वाली आवाज़ में चल सकें।

panels.shot: close-up of Bande Nawaz dictating, scribe writing
panels.action: A scribe with reed pen writes diligently on a manuscript while Bande Nawaz, eyes half-closed, dictates calmly, stacks of bound volumes nearby.

dialogue.text: In his Jawami-ul-Kilam, he gathered the sayings of Chishti elders. In his Dakhni works, he let the Deccan’s mixed tongue carry stories of love, humility and remembrance.

i18n.hi: जवामिउल कलाम में उन्होंने चिश्ती बुज़ुर्गों के क़ौल जमा किए। दख़नी लिखाई में उन्होंने दक्कन की मिली–जुली ज़बान को मोहब्बत, फ़ना और याद के किस्से उठाने दिए।

panels.shot: medium shot of scholars in debate in a hall
panels.action: Inside a simple hall, a group of sober-faced scholars sit opposite Bande Nawaz, some frowning thoughtfully as he speaks, a tension between deference and doubt in their posture.

dialogue.text: Yet his teaching on the unity of being stirred anxiety among some jurists. Ferishta notes debates around him, as stricter scholars worried about a path that dissolved sharp boundaries.

i18n.hi: लेकिन उनकी ‘वहदत अल-वजूद’ की बातें कुछ फ़ुक़हा के दिल में खटका डाल गईं। फ़िरिश्ता लिखता है, उनके आसपास बहसें उठीं, सख़्त उलेमा इन सीमाएँ पिघलाने वाले रास्तों से घबराए।

panels.shot: close-up on contemplative face, faintly weary but serene
panels.action: Bande Nawaz sits alone in the hospice at dusk, rosary in hand, the sounds of distant conversation and clatter from the kitchen faintly reaching him.

dialogue.speaker: bande_nawaz_gesudaraz
dialogue.text: Let them argue. The hungry do not debate when the pot is full.

i18n.hi: बहस करने दो, जब देग भर हो तो भूखे सवाल नहीं करते।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot of the khanqah evolving
panels.action: The khanqah complex appears in a wide shot, modest but expanding, as new wings, trees and graves gradually surround the original courtyard, with people flowing in and out.

dialogue.text: Over two decades in Gulbarga, his hospice became a small town of its own—kitchen, cells, a graveyard, classrooms—drawing villagers, officials and travelers into a shared rhythm.

i18n.hi: दो दशकों में गुलबर्गा में उनकी ख़ानकाह खुद एक छोटा कस्बा बन गई—रसोई, हुजरे, क़ब्रिस्तान, किताबख़ाना—जिसकी चाल में देहात, अमला और मुसाफ़िर सब शामिल हो गए।

panels.shot: somber interior shot near his resting place, late evening
panels.action: In the dim interior of a simple tomb chamber, Bande Nawaz lies in repose, wrapped in a plain shroud, while a few disciples sit quietly in prayer nearby.

dialogue.text: He died in 1422, far from the Delhi of his youth. But the hospice he built ensured that his absence did not empty the courtyard of food, counsel or song.

i18n.hi: १४२२ में वो अपने बचपन वाली दिल्ली से दूर दुनिया छोड़ गए। पर जो दरगाह उन्होंने खड़ी की, उसने उनकी ग़ैरहाज़िरी में भी आँगन से रोटी, मश्वरा और तराना कम न होने दिया।

panels.shot: modern-era wide shot of Gulbarga dargah complex
panels.action: Centuries later, the expanded dargah complex rises white and calm under the Deccan sun, with streams of visitors ascending its steps from different walks of life.

dialogue.text: Today, the dargah at Gulbarga stands where his hospice once fed and taught. Its stones remember an exile who turned a new city into home by serving whoever crossed his door.

i18n.hi: आज गुलबर्गा की दरगाह वहीं खड़ी है जहाँ उनकी ख़ानकाह कभी खिलाती और सिखाती थी। पत्थर आज भी उस मुहाजिर को याद रखते हैं जिसने हर आने-जाने वाले की ख़िदमत से पराए शहर को अपना घर कर दिया।
